lead: Textiles for the home – rugs, bedding, blankets, cushions, curtains and blinds, towels and table linen – organised by use, with collectable rugs and heritage textiles arranged by weaving tradition, then city or tribe, then version.

depts.note: Variety for hand-made rugs (tradition → city/tribe/workshop → antique, new or reproduction); tier for machine-made rugs and mats.

b.v: hand-knotted > hand-woven flatweave > hand-tufted > machine-woven (Wilton, Axminster) > machine-tufted
b.w: Construction sets durability and value of a rug.

b.v: silk > wool > synthetic
b.w: Material leads hand-made rugs.

b.v: 330+ knots per square inch very good > 120–330 medium to good > 80 or fewer poor
b.w: Knots per square inch rate the weave.

b.v: city or workshop; village; nomadic or tribal (a classification, not a ranking)
b.w: Dealers and auction houses catalogue rugs by origin first.
Dealers value natural over synthetic dyes.

b.v: antique (100+ years) > semi-antique > new; reproductions noted
b.w: Antique and rare pieces carry a premium.

b.v: EN 1307 use class
b.w: Machine-made rugs are rated by use class.

s.brief: One kind per weaving tradition; archetypes are city, regional or tribal weaves (the old Persian names on k29 become Persian-rug archetypes: Heriz, Tabriz, Kashan, Isfahan, Nain, Qom, Kerman, Sarouk, Bijar, Senneh, Hamadan, Mahal, Sultanabad, Serapi, Farahan, Qashqai, Bakhtiari, Afshar, Luri, Gabbeh, Baluchi, Mashad, Malayer, Zanjan, Ravar, Mehraban). Versions: antique / new / reproduction. Usak and Kayseri go to Anatolian. Add Caucasian (Kazak, Shirvan, Kuba, Karabagh, Gendje, Talish), Anatolian (Ushak, Hereke, Ladik, Konya, Milas, Bergama), Turkmen (Tekke, Yomut, Salor, Ersari, Saryk, Chodor; gul names), Afghan & Baluch, Chinese (Ningxia, Baotou, Peking, Art Deco/Nichols), Tibetan (Tibetan tiger rug, khaden), Indian & Pakistani (Agra, Amritsar, Jaipur, Lahore/Mughal). Add a tradition entry per tradition. Wilton/Axminster leave for the machine-made shelf.

k.brief: k29's machine-made types and Wilton/Axminster go to the Machine-made rug kind.
Turkish village and workshop rugs incl. Ushak, Hereke; include Usak, Kayseri from k29.

s.brief: Archetypes by named form and workshop: Moroccan Berber (Beni Ourain, Azilal, Boucherouite, Boujad, Kilim-hanbel), Aubusson and Savonnerie (French court carpets, reproductions), Scandinavian rya and rölakan, Spanish (Alpujarra, Cuenca), Polish/Arts & Crafts (Donegal, Morris & Co hand-knotted), modern designer rugs (Marimekko, Märta Måås-Fjetterström, Nanimarquina, The Rug Company, Kasthall). Traditions register entries for Moroccan, French court carpets, Scandinavian rya.

k.brief: Scandinavian long-pile rya and related ryijy (Finland).
Donegal, Morris & Co, Spanish Alpujarra/Cuenca and similar.
Named 20th-c./contemporary designer and studio rugs; archetypes by designer.

s.brief: Flatweaves as archetypes of the Flatweave rug kind: kilim (Anatolian, Persian, Balkan Pirot/Chiprovtsi), soumak, dhurrie, jijim/cicim, zili, verneh, rölakan. Navajo weaving as its own kind (Two Grey Hills, Ganado Red, Teec Nos Pos, Chief's blanket phases, Germantown, Yei). Hooked rugs (Grenfell, Waldoboro, Cheticamp). Felt: shyrdak, ala kiyiz, felt-ball. Rag: trasmatta, braided rag rug. Hide: cowhide, sheepskin, reindeer. Traditions: kilim, Navajo, Kyrgyz felt (shyrdak is UNESCO ICH).

Tier: machine-made rugs (Wilton, Axminster, machine-tufted, flatwoven, washable, outdoor) as types of one new kind; market-covering makers (e.g. IKEA, Ruggable, Safavieh, Loloi, Nourison, Brink & Campman) plus test winners only. Rug pad stays kind-level with a few makers.

k.brief: Types: Wilton, Axminster, tufted, flatwoven, washable, outdoor.

s.brief: Restraint: plain definitions, few or no models; meditation mat moves to Cushions.

depts.note: Tier for everyday bedding; variety for luxury linen houses and heritage quilts and blankets.

b.v: extra-long-staple cotton, linen, silk > long-staple > short-staple and blends
b.w: Fibre leads bed-linen quality.

b.v: percale; sateen; renforcé; jersey; flannel; finishes such as singeing and mercerising are a choice
b.w: Weave sets the feel; finishing adds quality.

b.v: single > multi-ply
b.w: Single-ply yarn is the better construction.

b.v: weak above about 400; counting plies inflates it
b.w: Weighed last.

b.v: down fill power: about 900 best goose down > 600 > about 300 feathers
b.w: Fill decides duvets and pillows.

b.v: by season, not a quality rank
b.w: Season is a filter on bedding.

s.brief: Tier mainstream plus luxury linen houses as brands/ranges: Frette, Sferra, Pratesi, Libeco, Matouk, Yves Delorme, Porthault, Anichini, Garnier-Thiebaut; Hästens bed linen (the Hästens mattress is Furniture). Weave (percale, sateen, linen, flannel, jersey) as types. Brand-register entries for the luxury houses. Cut Solace SKU; add test winners (Wirecutter/Which?/CHOICE).

Duvets/comforters tier (fill types; down makers such as Brinkhaus, Hanskruchen, Cuddledown, Snowe; test winners). Quilts as variety by tradition: Amish, Gee's Bend, Hawaiian, Baltimore album, crazy quilt, Welsh quilt, Durham/North Country quilt, Bengali kantha, Japanese sashiko, Indian ralli; patterns (Log Cabin, Double Wedding Ring, Lone Star) as archetypes. Bedspreads: candlewick, Marseilles/matelassé, chenille, Indian block-printed. Traditions register: kantha, Gee's Bend, Amish quilts, Welsh/North Country quilting.

Heritage blankets as archetypes: Hudson's Bay point blanket, Pendleton (Chief Joseph, Glacier Park, trade blankets), Welsh tapestry/caernarfon blankets (Melin Tregwynt, Trefriw), Faribault, Johnstons of Elgin, Avoca, Klippan, Lapuan Kankurit, Mexican sarape/Saltillo, Andean manta. Weighted blanket as a type. Electric blanket tier (Sunbeam, Dreamland, Silentnight, Beurer). Swaddle with blankets (keep baby tag). Traditions register: Welsh weaving, Pendleton/trade blanket, HBC point blanket.

k.brief: Wool, cotton cellular, fleece, weighted as types; heritage archetypes.
Keep tg baby; muslin, wrap and sleep-sack types.

s.brief: Restraint: fill and shape as types (down, feather, memory foam, latex, buckwheat; orthopaedic, body pillow); few market-covering makers.
Restraint: one entry per layer; trim Bedgear SKU list to the brand; pillow protector joins the protectors.

b.v: 20,000 rubs for domestic use
b.w: How long cover fabric lasts.

b.v: grade 1–5
b.w: Pilling follows rub resistance.

s.brief: Restraint: plain definitions; meditation cushion and mat sit together; no SKU lists.
Restraint: fitted (per model) and stretch/throw-over as types; drop IKEA model SKUs.

b.v: blackout; thermal; unlined
b.w: Lining sets light and heat control.

b.v: 20,000 rubs for domestic use
b.w: How long curtain fabric lasts.

b.v: EN 13120 / cordless
b.w: Looped cords are a known strangulation hazard.

s.brief: Restraint: heading styles (pencil pleat, eyelet, tab top, pinch pleat) as types.
Restraint: plain definitions; blackout, motorised as types.
Merge curtain hardware: brackets and finials into the pole; rings, hooks, gliders and tiebacks into one fittings kind.

k.brief: Rings, hooks, gliders, tiebacks and holdbacks as types.

depts.note: Tier for everyday towels; variety for luxury terry makers and flat-woven traditions.

b.v: Egyptian/Supima/Turkish long-staple cotton, linen > standard cotton > blends
b.w: Towels are judged by fibre first.

b.v: bands held until a fetched page shows them
b.w: Towel weight follows fibre.

s.brief: Towel sizes stay as types. Luxury makers as brands (Abyss & Habidecor, Frette, Christy, Kassatex, Matouk, Sferra, Uchino/Imabari towels); test winners (Wirecutter/Which?). Flat-woven: Turkish peshtemal (Buldan, Denizli), Finnish/Lapuan linen sauna towel, Japanese tenugui. Carry cloth: furoshiki and bojagi as archetypes. Traditions: Imabari towels, peshtemal weaving, bojagi.

depts.note: Trim the IKEA-only lists; add linen houses and table-linen traditions.

b.v: linen > cotton-linen > cotton > polyester
b.w: Fibre decides hand, absorbency and wear.

s.brief: Cut IKEA SKUs to at most one range per kind. Add makers: Garnier-Thiebaut, Le Jacquard Français, Libeco, Linum, Ulster Weavers, Thomas Ferguson (Irish linen damask), Jacquard Basque houses (Lartigue 1910), Lapuan Kankurit. Archetypes: damask tablecloth, Basque linen (stripes), Provençal indienne, Indian block print, Irish linen tea towel, Japanese tenugui/kitchen cloth. Traditions: Irish linen, Basque linen, Indian block printing (Bagru/Sanganer).
